title: Nothing bare on the popup — Sound, About, Performance, Shortcuts

steps.headline: Sound: better as cards?
steps.changed: Volume and Notification each sit in a card, like Remote Access. The tabs, the on/off switch and the sound list are one card, because they are one idea.
steps.notice: Only grouping changes. The sound list keeps its 8px gaps; nothing is removed.

steps.headline: About: better as cards?
steps.changed: Version and the two policy links share the first card (the links are outlined buttons now, not underlined text). Disclaimer, Privacy and Licenses each sit in a card. The long privacy parts and the library list fold open. The usage-stats switch stays visible.
steps.notice: Every sentence is the approved wording, unchanged — only where it sits. New words are only the fold titles: "Your account (optional)", "Friends & presence (optional)", "Anonymous usage stats", "Remote access and games", "Open-source libraries". The underline under Disclaimer/Privacy/Licenses goes, since the text is now inside cards.

steps.headline: Performance: better as cards?
steps.changed: One card holds the power-saving switch, the restart notice when it shows, and your detected graphics chips. A "How GPU choice works" card holds the explanation, with its three sections folded — the popup now opens short. The spaced-capital heading is gone.
steps.notice: The one-line intro "GPU choice affects performance." is removed — it repeated the explanation. Every other word is unchanged.

steps.headline: Keyboard Shortcuts: better as cards?
steps.changed: The shortcut table sits in a card instead of bare on the popup.
steps.notice: Three longer descriptions now wrap onto two lines — the card's padding costs a little width in this fixed-width popup.
